title: Network ACL Changes

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.61 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.61 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="ec2.amazonaws.com" (eventName="CreateNetworkAclEntry" OR eventName="ReplaceNetworkAclEntry" OR eventName="DeleteNetworkAclEntry")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.61_network_acl_changes_61"
| sort -_time
description: NACL changes can open subnets to the internet or break least-privilege segmentation; they are less common than security groups and warrant explicit audit.
value: Detecting network acl changes early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Require change tickets in deployment pipeline metadata where possible. Alert on any prod NACL change. Visualize before/after rule numbers and CIDR blocks from `requestParameters`. Weekly review with network team.
visualization: Table (NACL, user, action), Timeline (changes), Single value (changes 24h).
cimSpl: | tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Change.All_Changes by All_Changes.user | sort - count
dataModelAcceleration: Change (All_Changes): for CloudTrail management events mapped to CIM. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Automation that refreshes the same NACL or SG rule during migration; change ticket should name the CIDRs.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Require change tickets in deployment pipeline metadata where possible. Alert on any prod NACL change. Visualize before/after rule numbers and CIDR blocks from `requestParameters`. Weekly review with network team.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="ec2.amazonaws.com" (eventName="CreateNetworkAclEntry" OR eventName="ReplaceNetworkAclEntry" OR eventName="DeleteNetworkAclEntry")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.61_network_acl_changes_61"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect network acl changes. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_61_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (NACL, user, action), Timeline (changes), Single value (changes 24h)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of network acl changes so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
